title: Introduction
summary: The introduction establishes the motivation for Artificial Collective Intelligence (ACI) and highlights that existing experimentation platforms and multi-agent RL algorithms are limited to dozens of agents, creating a need for a platform supporting large-scale multi-agent RL.

title: The MAgent Platform
summary: MAgent is introduced as a highly scalable many-agent reinforcement learning platform capable of hosting up to one million agents on a single GPU, featuring flexible environment/agent configuration, a reward description language, and interactive visualization tools.

title: Gridworld Fundamentals
summary: The gridworld serves as the fundamental environment, where agents have rectangular bodies with local and optional global perspectives, and can perform moving, turning, or attacking actions; a C++ engine supports fast simulation of heterogeneous agents with configurable state/action spaces.

title: Reward Description Language
summary: A reward description language in Python allows users to define rewards, agent symbols, and events using boolean expressions with logical operations, assigning rewards to agents involved when event conditions are met.

title: Baseline Algorithms
summary: Baseline algorithms implemented include parameter-sharing DQN, DRQN, and A2C, with DQN performing best; an embedding is trained for each agent's unique ID to introduce diversity, and users can benchmark their algorithms against these baselines.

title: Live and Interactive Part
summary: The demo showcases three example games—pursuit, gathering, and battle—demonstrating emergent behaviors such as local cooperation in pursuit and competition in resource-limited gathering environments, with an interactive renderer for exploration.

title: Battle shows the hybrid of cooperation and competition.
summary: The battle scenario features two armies of hundreds of agents that learn both global and local strategies like encirclement attack and guerrilla warfare through self-play; a human player interface allows visitors to control agents alongside RL agents.

title: Conclusion
summary: The conclusion describes MAgent as a research platform for studying many-agent RL at both individual and societal levels, with future work planned to support continuous environments and provide additional algorithms.
